issues.reason: Compound concepts states the head genus is "always emitted either way" for a modifier_noun compound whose last word is a real head noun, and a lantern-keeper is a keeper, so the mandatory `(Inheritance lantern_keeper keeper)` is simply absent.

The proper-noun-premodifier rule (parse the head noun normally, link it with the opaque `Possession`) and the capitalized-plural-label rule prescribe different routes for a CAPITALIZED head and nothing subordinates one to the other, and both emitted atoms are true and well-typed — `Possession` is expressly the loose-association licence and `keeper` is read straight off the head noun — so this is licensed improvisation in gap territory.

gaps_confirmed: a proper noun premodifying a CAPITALIZED plural common-noun head ("Aelmere Keepers"): the proper-noun-premodifier rule and the capitalized-run-exceeds-the-class-word / Name-only-plural-label rule give conflicting routes and the instruction set names no selector
new_gaps: if the Name-only route is the one intended for "Aelmere Keepers", a bare-plural GENERIC verbal clause about that label has no licensed form at all: a Name-only individual is not a kind, so it cannot range an `Implication`, and a habitual "exchange letters" would have to collapse into a single unmarked event on that individual — a licensed form would need to carry kind-hood and name-hood on one symbol
defect_summary: Add the mandatory head genus `(: lk_genus (Inheritance lantern_keeper keeper) (STV 1.0 0.99))` beside the existing capability and kind-relation atoms; nothing else in the parse changes.
notes: The agent-nominalization atoms are licensed because `lantern_keeper` was fused from the surface, and the noun modifier is correctly left unexposed. The "Aelmere Keepers" routing is a live doctrine conflict, not a parse fault.
